questions.q: What is the one hard requirement for ledgers to be grouped into the same ledger set?
options: They must share the same chart of accounts and the same calendar or period type combination
They must all use the same currency
They must all belong to the same business unit
They must all be secondary ledgers
questions.explain: Every member of a ledger set must share an identical chart of accounts and calendar/period type combination; currency can still differ.

questions.q: Which ledger types can be members of a ledger set?
options: Only primary ledgers
Primary ledgers, secondary ledgers, and reporting currencies, as long as they share chart of accounts and calendar
Only business units
Only legal entities
questions.explain: A ledger set can include any combination of primary ledgers, secondary ledgers, and reporting currencies that meet the chart-of-accounts-and-calendar requirement.

questions.q: What two categories of work does a ledger set primarily simplify?
options: Journal approval workflow routing
Supplier invoice entry and payment processing
Period opening/closing and reporting across multiple ledgers at once
Legal entity registration and address management
questions.explain: Ledger sets let you open/close periods once across every member and run many reports across the whole set in one pass.

questions.q: Does a ledger set merge the balances of its member ledgers into one combined accounting entity?
options: Only if all members are primary ledgers
Only for reporting currencies, never for primary ledgers
Yes, that is exactly what defines a ledger set
No — each member ledger keeps its own currency, legal entity assignments, and balances
questions.explain: A ledger set is a management and reporting convenience; it does not merge member ledgers' underlying balances into a single entity.

questions.q: How does a ledger set differ from a secondary ledger?
options: They are the same thing with different names
A secondary ledger creates a new, potentially different accounting representation of one primary ledger; a ledger set groups already-identical ledgers to save repetitive work
A ledger set always requires a different chart of accounts; a secondary ledger never does
A secondary ledger cannot be assigned a calendar
questions.explain: A secondary ledger can differ in chart of accounts, calendar, or currency to add a new accounting view, while a ledger set groups structurally identical ledgers purely for convenience.
